gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-days-one: Chunky, glowing headlines meet a body with rungs of generous spacing. Wallpoet lets paper show through its lines, while Days One fills each line with a big, friendly plain sans that moves along smoothly.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-epunda-sans: Commanding from the first word, Wallpoet rises tall with smooth curves and open lines. Epunda Sans follows in oversized, daylight-filled counters, a sans that stays out of the way and lets the heading talk.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-farro: Farro reads like a single thread of ink, snug and uniform, with short ascenders. Wallpoet is best when its tall, see-through letters get to show off, while Farro does its finest work by simply carrying the words along.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-fragment-mono: Precise and structured, the body sets its letters out like nails on a ruler. Fragment Mono keeps a tidy, tubing-like line going, while Wallpoet handles the loud, tall, light-through-the-gaps display work.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-geist-mono: Technical in feel, the body text marches in fixed-width steps beneath a bold, commanding heading. Geist Mono draws each letter with pen-like steadiness and wide side gaps, which gives Wallpoet's tall, see-through shapes something orderly to stand over.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-genos: Tall, bold, and see-through: that's Wallpoet, with smooth bends and lowercase that climbs. And Genos brings a tight, contemporary sans with a high midline and barely-varying strokes, doing the steady reading work the heading never could.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-geom: Wallpoet looks like a commanding sign with paper showing between its tall, smooth-bending letters, over a body with a lofty lowercase band. It earns its keep big and short.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-hammersmith-one: Loud, see-through headlines sit over a body drawn like cut lengths of cord. And Hammersmith One keeps its capitals close to lowercase height and has no hairlines to squint at, so Wallpoet gets all the drama.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-inder: Commanding Wallpoet stands tall, its smooth bends letting the paper peek through between letters. But Inder keeps its capitals and lowercase close in height, a clean plain sans that gives the heading room to be loud.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-jaldi: Big, brushed-looking body text meets a tall, see-through heading with smooth bends. Yet the strongest single quality here is Jaldi's lifted x-height and gaping c, a sans-serif that holds its own beside Wallpoet.
